newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU makes new rice import offer to U.S..
newsitem.headline: EU makes new rice import offer to U.S..

text.p: The European Commission has offered the U.S. a revised draft regulation on brown rice imports in a bid to break an 18-month trade dispute over cumulative tariff recovery, a Commission official said on Friday.
The European Union cereals experts group was meeting all day on Friday before talks between the Commission and trade officials in Washington, due to start in the late afternoon.

The dispute arises from a complaint filed to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Geneva in September 1995 over a Commission plan to allow rice importers and exporters to reclaim tariffs overpaid on a cumulative basis.

"The Commission based their proposal on the question of fraud but the U.S. has a legal code and a tough code of practice and feels that brown rice exports should be based on the invoice price like every other product," a U.S. source said.
The new proposal is unlikely to satisfy Washington but EU member states will have a bigger problem accepting the new proposal, the source said.
The European Commission refused to comment on the progress of the discussions.
